result.summary: This pull request modifies `test/fuzz/test_runner.py` to split fuzz corpora into shards matching `--par` by default, allowing single fuzz targets or unevenly sized corpora to execute across multiple worker processes. It also updates `ci/test/02_run_container.py` to mount tmpfs and APFS ramdisks to mitigate disk I/O bottlenecks caused by shard directory creation.
result.problem: When running the fuzz test runner with `--par`, single targets cannot be parallelized, and parallel multi-target runs are constrained by the runtime of the slowest single target.

open_concerns: Sharded runs fragment libFuzzer coverage metrics in the summary output so coverage cannot be easily compared across runs
Target setup overhead and hard link file operations can cause storage thrashing on platforms without fast tmpfs
resolved_concerns: Temporary directories left behind on abort or colliding across jobs were addressed by creating per-job temporary directories and adding CI tmpfs/ramdisk mounts

categories.name: tests
categories.evidence: Touches test/fuzz/test_runner.py to add corpus sharding support to the fuzz test infrastructure.
categories.rationale: corpus sharding speeds up individual target fuzz validation significantly when running on multi-core systems, solving the long-tail runner bottleneck where one target dominates total elapsed test time. However, it incurs storage overhead and breaks target-wide aggregated coverage figures, making it a worthwhile enhancement that can be deferred.

result.card: This PR updates the fuzz test runner to divide target corpora into shards so that single targets and long-tail targets can execute across multiple cores during parallel runs. It also introduces tmpfs and ramdisk mounts in the CI container runner to minimize disk link overhead. Measurements show 7 to 15 minute speedups on sanitized and Windows CI jobs, though macOS gains are limited by test setup costs and corpus sharding fragments per-target coverage totals. Review is active following a Concept ACK and revisions by the author.
